title.narrative: Improved access to municipal and social services through renewable energy alternatives and provision of support to Zahle basic services to enhance preparedness and crisis response capacities to protect communities and respond to conflict and natural disas

description.narrative:
The project aims to enhance the wellbeing, safety, health, and security conditions of both host and refugee populations in Zahle Beqa’a, Lebanon. This will be achieved by improving the operations of public facilities and enhancing safety in targeted communities through reliable and renewable energy supplies to these facilities and public spaces. Lebanon, hosting the highest number of refugees per capita globally, has a severely strained energy sector and collapsing social services. The project addresses urgent needs under Lebanon's Emergency Response Plan for 2021-2022, particularly in the WaSH and health sectors, by providing reliable energy to facilities like Tel Chiha Hospital and a Beqa’a Water Establishment pumping station during the first phase of the project. Renewable energy systems, designed by experts in coordination with the Lebanese Center for Energy Conservation, will ensure consistent power for essential services. A technical committee comprising UN-Habitat, local government, LCEC, consultants, and community members will oversee the project’s implementation. Given Lebanon's severe socio-economic, political, and energy crises, exacerbated by the Syrian refugee influx, Beirut Port explosion, COVID-19, and recent Gaza conflict spill-over, public sector services have drastically deteriorated.
The average salary within the public sector went down from US$ 1,000 to at most US$ 40. This has significantly impacted the quantity and quality of services provided by public institutions where public-sector employees stopped showing up to work as their wages can barely cover transportation. This comes against the backdrop of the Syrian refugee crisis which continues to pressure existing malfunctioning and overburdened urban services and municipalities, the Beirut Port explosion, the lasting COVID-19 pandemic impact – and more recently and urgently, the drastic armed conflict spill-over effect of the war in Gaza, on Lebanon.
The departments and branches of the Civil Defence were heavily impacted by funding cuts imposed by the central government, thus severely impacting their ability to respond and provide emergency services. Based on a UN-Habitat rapid survey, around 80% of the CD fleet is non-functional due to the lack of maintenance while the remaining 20% is not utilized due to lack of fuel. Despite all these constraints, the CD remains one of the only public institutions that still responds to emergency needs of the community, both in urban and rural settings – while other public sectors have ceased to function. However, the deteriorated ability of the CD across Lebanon, to adequately and efficiently respond to emergencies has led an increase in fatalities as well as loss of infrastructural and environmental assets across the country.
Consequently, with the funding made available for the second phase, the project will rehabilitate and equip the Zahle District CD to strengthen its civil protection, prevention, and preparedness capacities to better respond to potential emergency needs caused by the impact of conflict, manmade and natural hazards that might turn into disasters. The need for their services is even more apparent in the preparedness context of the country and steps taken by the UN in line with the Government, to the ongoing and likely protracted spill over impact of the war in Gaza in the South of Lebanon which is already causing vast material damage and human loss.
Thus, based on a rapid survey conducted by UN-Habitat to identify CD current urgent needs and challenges in Lebanon, the project will upgrade the building, its basic services, mainly water and sanitation, repair essential trucks and vehicles, and provide personnel firefighting/emergency response tools and equipment.
The project approach will validate the previous assessment of the CD centre in Zahle, with additional technical assessments on urgent needs. This includes an assessment of the physical situation of the centre in terms of rehabilitation of the building, the current situation of firefighting trucks and vehicles, and the last assessment will cover the personnel protection gear needed to fight fires and respond to other emergencies in a safe and efficient way. The main expected accomplishment is a vastly improved CD centre that is better able to respond to emergencies, covering not only the large district of Zahle and neighbouring municipalities. In addition to the improved coordination mechanism created by the awareness raising workshops between the CD and the surrounding municipalities. It will also serve as a strong facility that can support the country better cope with the potential impact of a spreading conflict from the south to the rest of the country or dispatch its capacities south to support.
